title: AI Leaders Library
description: Curated resources for executives, directors, board members and engineering leaders learning how AI is used in business.

resources.title: One Useful Thing
resources.author: Ethan Mollick (Wharton)
resources.description: Regular essays on what the newest models can actually do and how that changes work, management and teaching. Written for non-technical leaders and consistently ahead of the mainstream press.

resources.title: An opinionated guide to which AI to use (Summer 2026)
resources.author: Ethan Mollick, July 2026
resources.description: Plain advice on choosing between ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, which tier is worth paying for, and how to use the new agent modes without handing over too much control. Updated periodically.

resources.title: Co-Intelligence: Living and Working with AI
resources.author: Ethan Mollick, Portfolio, 2024
resources.description: A short book on treating AI as a colleague, tutor and coach, with four working rules for using it well. A good first book for an executive who has used ChatGPT a little and wants a mental model.

resources.title: Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier
resources.author: Dell'Acqua, Mollick, Lakhani et al. (HBS / BCG), 2023
resources.description: The field experiment with BCG consultants: on tasks within AI's capability, consultants using GPT-4 were faster and produced better work; on a task just outside it, they did worse. The source of the 'jagged frontier' idea that most AI adoption thinking now leans on.

resources.title: AI For Everyone
resources.author: Andrew Ng, DeepLearning.AI on Coursera
resources.description: About 7 hours. Non-technical grounding in what AI can and cannot do, how to choose projects, and how to build an AI team. Predates the generative AI wave but the project-selection material still holds.

resources.title: Generative AI for Everyone
resources.author: Andrew Ng, DeepLearning.AI on Coursera
resources.description: About 6 hours. How generative AI works, where it fits in a business, and how to think about its effect on jobs and tasks. The natural follow-on to AI For Everyone.

resources.title: Large Language Models explained briefly
resources.author: 3Blue1Brown (Grant Sanderson), 2024
resources.description: A short animated explainer made for the Computer History Museum. The clearest few minutes available on what an LLM is doing when it answers a question.

resources.title: Intro to Large Language Models
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy, 2023
resources.description: A one-hour talk for a general audience from a founding member of OpenAI. Covers how models are trained, what they are good and bad at, and a useful section on security risks such as jailbreaks and prompt injection.

resources.title: How I use LLMs
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy, 2025
resources.description: Two hours of an expert's real daily use: search, file uploads, deep research, voice, coding and choosing a model per task. Watch at 1.5x and skip to the sections you need.

resources.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
resources.author: Andrej Karpathy, 2025
resources.description: A three and a half hour walkthrough of how LLMs are built: pre-training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and why models hallucinate. No code, but demanding. For leaders who need to hold their own with engineers.

resources.title: AI Fluency: Framework & Foundations
resources.author: Anthropic Academy, with UCC and Ringling College
resources.description: A short course on working with AI effectively and responsibly: when to delegate to it, how to describe a task, how to judge the output. Model-agnostic despite the publisher. Includes an assessment and certificate.

resources.title: Anthropic Academy
resources.author: Anthropic
resources.description: Anthropic's learning hub, with tracks for using Claude at work and for building with the API, MCP and Claude Code. Useful as a single place to point mixed teams.

resources.title: OpenAI Academy
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.description: Courses, live sessions and recordings grouped by audience. The 'Lead AI Adoption' track for leaders covers AI strategy and building an adoption roadmap. Requires a free account.

resources.title: Google AI Essentials
resources.author: Google, on Coursera
resources.description: Five modules, under 5 hours, aimed at everyday workplace use: prompting, drafting, analysis and responsible use. Good for rolling out to a whole leadership team. Coursera subscription required.

resources.title: Gemini for Google Workspace: Prompting Guide 101
resources.author: Google, 2024
resources.description: A 45-page PDF of worked prompts organised by role, including a section for executives. The persona, task, context and format structure transfers to any assistant.

resources.title: Microsoft Copilot Scenario Library
resources.author: Microsoft Adoption
resources.description: Use cases for Microsoft 365 Copilot, browsable by function (Finance, HR, Sales, Legal, Marketing) and by industry. Useful for running a use-case workshop in a Microsoft shop.

resources.title: AI in the Enterprise: Lessons from seven frontier companies
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.description: A 24-page PDF of adoption lessons from companies such as Morgan Stanley and Klarna: start with evals, embed AI in products, invest early, unblock developers. Vendor-written, so read it as a playbook from one side of the table.

resources.title: Identifying and scaling AI use cases
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.description: A 33-page PDF that sorts use cases into six types and gives an impact versus effort framework for prioritising them. A practical template for a first use-case portfolio.

resources.title: The Gen AI Playbook for Organizations
resources.author: Bharat Anand and Andy Wu, Harvard Business Review, Nov 2025
resources.description: A framework for deciding which tasks to give to generative AI, based on how costly an error would be and whether the task rests on facts or judgement. Good material for a board or executive discussion.

resources.title: Competing in the Age of AI
resources.author: Marco Iansiti and Karim Lakhani, Harvard Business Review, 2020
resources.description: The argument that firms built around data and AI scale in ways traditional operating models cannot. Written before generative AI; the operating-model thesis has aged well. Expanded into a book of the same name.

resources.title: Building effective agents
resources.author: Anthropic Engineering, Dec 2024
resources.description: The most-cited short piece on when to use a simple workflow and when to use an autonomous agent, with the common design patterns. Essential for anyone approving agent projects.

resources.title: A practical guide to building agents
resources.author: OpenAI
resources.description: A 33-page PDF for product and engineering leads: picking agent use cases, models, tools, orchestration and guardrails. Pairs well with the Anthropic piece above.

resources.title: Prompt engineering overview
resources.author: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs)
resources.description: Official documentation on writing effective prompts, with links to best practices and interactive tutorials. Most of the advice applies to any model.

resources.title: Anthropic courses (GitHub)
resources.author: Anthropic
resources.description: Jupyter notebook courses on the API, prompt engineering, prompt evaluation and tool use. Hands-on and code-based; for leaders who want to build something themselves or understand what their teams are doing.

resources.title: DeepLearning.AI short courses
resources.author: Andrew Ng and partners
resources.description: Over 100 courses of one to two hours each, mostly built with vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, LangChain and others). Ranges from business overviews to building agents and retrieval systems.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Course
resources.author: Hugging Face
resources.description: A free course on working with open models: transformers, fine-tuning and deployment, with Colab notebooks. For technical leaders evaluating open-weight models alongside commercial APIs.

resources.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
resources.author: fast.ai
resources.description: Nine lessons of about 90 minutes plus a book and notebooks. Assumes you can code. Included for technical executives who want a real foundation in how models are trained.

resources.title: Elements of AI
resources.author: University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn
resources.description: A self-paced introduction for non-experts, available in many European languages. Part 1 needs no maths or coding. Predates generative AI but gives solid general literacy.

resources.title: AI For Business Specialization
resources.author: Wharton (University of Pennsylvania), on Coursera
resources.description: Four courses, about 44 hours in total, on AI in marketing, finance, people management and strategy, plus ethics and governance. A structured option for functional leaders.

resources.title: Artificial Intelligence: Implications for Business Strategy
resources.author: MIT Sloan and MIT CSAIL (online, via GetSmarter)
resources.description: Six weeks at six to eight hours a week, covering AI technologies and how to build a business strategy around them. Listed at around US$3,850; check current dates and price.

resources.title: AI for Boards
resources.author: INSEAD Executive Education
resources.description: A four-day in-person programme at Fontainebleau for directors, covering AI oversight, risk and strategy at board level. Around €11,600.

resources.title: AI Governance in the Boardroom
resources.author: Institute of Directors (UK), June 2025
resources.description: Twelve principles, revised in 2025, laid out as the questions a board should be asking about AI. Short enough to take straight into a board meeting.

resources.title: A Director's Guide to AI Governance (v2)
resources.author: Australian Institute of Company Directors and UTS Human Technology Institute, June 2026
resources.description: A thorough director-level guide with a separate checklist for smaller organisations and not-for-profits. Australian, though most of it applies anywhere.

resources.title: AI Risk Management Framework
resources.author: NIST (US)
resources.description: The reference framework for managing AI risk (govern, map, measure, manage), with a 2024 profile specific to generative AI. Being revised in 2026. The base most corporate AI risk policies are built on.

resources.title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 AI management systems
resources.author: ISO / IEC
resources.description: The certifiable international standard for running an AI management system, in the same family as ISO 27001. Relevant when customers or regulators start asking for certification.

resources.title: EU Artificial Intelligence Act: developments and analyses
resources.author: Future of Life Institute
resources.description: An independent site with the full text of the Act, an implementation timeline, an SME guide and a compliance checker. The fastest way to find out which obligations apply to you.

resources.title: Artificial intelligence guidance
resources.author: Information Commissioner's Office (UK)
resources.description: The UK regulator's guidance on AI and data protection, explaining AI-assisted decisions, and an AI risk toolkit. Required reading for any UK business putting personal data through AI.

resources.title: AI Playbook for the UK Government
resources.author: Government Digital Service, Feb 2025
resources.description: Ten principles and practical guidance for using AI safely in government. Written for the public sector but a well-structured model for any organisation's internal AI policy.

resources.title: Guidelines for secure AI system development
resources.author: NCSC (UK) and CISA (US), 2023
resources.description: Security guidance across design, development, deployment and operation, endorsed by agencies from 18 countries. Give it to whoever owns security for your AI projects.

resources.title: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (2025)
resources.author: OWASP GenAI Security Project
resources.description: The ten main security risks in LLM applications, from prompt injection to excessive agency and unbounded consumption. The checklist security teams use; leaders should know the names.

resources.title: Prompt injection (series)
resources.author: Simon Willison
resources.description: Posts from the person who named the attack, explaining why AI agents that read untrusted content can be hijacked and why there is still no complete fix. The clearest account of the main security limit on agents.

resources.title: AI Hero
resources.author: Matt Pocock
resources.description: Matt Pocock's site on AI engineering for professional developers: free articles on agent workflows (plan mode, AGENTS.md, tracer bullets, Ralph loops), an AI coding dictionary, free installable skills and a free email course. The hub for everything below.

resources.title: Tracer Bullets: Keeping AI Slop Under Control
resources.author: Matt Pocock, AI Hero
resources.description: How to get coding agents to build a thin end-to-end slice first and grow it, so problems surface early and the agent produces less code you then have to unpick. A good example of classic engineering discipline applied to agents.

resources.title: Skills for Real Engineers
resources.author: Matt Pocock (GitHub)
resources.description: An MIT-licensed set of small, composable agent skills that push coding agents through planning, specs, TDD and review: grill-me, to-spec, to-tickets, tdd, code-review, improve-codebase-architecture and more. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and Gemini CLI. Also available as a Claude Code plugin.

resources.title: AI Coding Crash Course
resources.author: Matt Pocock, AI Hero
resources.description: Self-paced, nearly 60 lessons. How agent harnesses like Claude Code work, managing the context window, AGENTS.md, skills, subagents and breaking work into session-sized chunks. US$299, team licences available.

resources.title: AI Coding for Real Engineers
resources.author: Matt Pocock, AI Hero
resources.description: A two-week cohort course (5 to 8 hours a week) on using coding agents on production codebases: PRDs and multi-phase plans, feedback loops with CI and red-green-refactor, and moving from supervised to autonomous agent loops. Runs periodically; join the waitlist for the next cohort.

resources.title: AI Skills with Matt Pocock
resources.author: The Pragmatic Engineer (Gergely Orosz), Sep 2026
resources.description: A conversation on why software fundamentals matter more when every agent session starts from nothing: context management, tracer bullets, TDD with agents, and cloud versus local agents. Also on video.

resources.title: Modern Software Engineering (YouTube channel)
resources.author: Dave Farley (formerly the Continuous Delivery channel)
resources.description: Weekly videos from the co-author of Continuous Delivery on engineering practice, deployment pipelines, TDD and team organisation, with a steady stream of evidence-led takes on AI-assisted development and vibe coding.

resources.title: We Studied 150 Developers Using AI (Here's What's Actually Changed)
resources.author: Dave Farley, Jan 2026
resources.description: Farley presents the results of the controlled study he co-authored (below) on what AI assistants do to developer speed and to the maintainability of the code they produce. Short enough to show an executive team asking about productivity claims.

resources.title: Echoes of AI: Downstream Effects of AI Assistants on Software Maintainability
resources.author: Borg, Farley et al., 2025 (revised Feb 2026)
resources.description: A two-phase study with 151 participants, mostly professional developers. AI users were markedly faster in the first phase; when other developers later had to change that code, there was no clear maintainability penalty or benefit. Flags code bloat and 'cognitive debt' as open risks.

resources.title: Safe production changes with agents
resources.author: LeadDev panel with Dave Farley, Heidi Waterhouse and Jean du Plessis, June 2026
resources.description: A panel on keeping software releasable when agents write much of the code: automated pipelines and guardrails, provenance and ownership at AI speed, and bringing agents into the delivery lifecycle in a controlled way. Free LeadDev account required.

resources.title: Modern Software Engineering
resources.author: David Farley, Addison-Wesley (Pearson), 2021
resources.description: Farley's case for engineering as optimising for learning and for managing complexity: small steps, fast feedback, testability, modularity. Written before coding agents, and the principles are exactly what makes AI-generated code safe to ship.

resources.title: AI Index Report 2026
resources.author: Stanford HAI
resources.description: The annual data-heavy picture of AI: model performance, cost, investment, adoption, regulation and public opinion. Use the summary chapter for board packs.

resources.title: The state of AI in 2026
resources.author: McKinsey / QuantumBlack, Aug 2026
resources.description: The annual global survey of how companies are adopting AI and whether it is showing up in the numbers. Useful for benchmarking your own organisation against peers.

resources.title: AI eats the world (Spring 2026)
resources.author: Benedict Evans
resources.description: An independent analyst's annual slide deck on where AI is going and what it means for the technology industry and everyone else. Sceptical where it should be.

resources.title: Work Trend Index 2026
resources.author: Microsoft WorkLab, May 2026
resources.description: Microsoft's annual survey of how AI and agents are changing knowledge work, team structure and management. Vendor research, but a large sample.

resources.title: Anthropic Economic Index
resources.author: Anthropic
resources.description: Ongoing research on which occupations and tasks people use AI for, and whether they use it to help or hand work over completely. Based on real usage data rather than surveys.

resources.title: AI as Normal Technology
resources.author: Arvind Narayanan and Sayash Kapoor (Princeton)
resources.description: Formerly AI Snake Oil. A careful counterweight to the hype: AI as a powerful technology whose effects arrive slowly, through adoption and institutions. Good for testing vendor claims.

resources.title: AI 2027
resources.author: Kokotajlo, Alexander, Larsen, Lifland and Dean
resources.description: A detailed forecast scenario of rapid progress towards superhuman AI. Contested, and best read alongside AI as Normal Technology to see both ends of the debate leaders are being asked to plan across.

resources.title: How I AI
resources.author: Lenny's Newsletter
resources.description: Executives and practitioners screen-share their actual AI workflows, such as a CEO's personal AI stack or a product leader's AI chief of staff. Concrete ideas you can copy the same day.

resources.title: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
resources.author: Google
resources.description: Load board papers, reports or contracts and ask questions that are answered only from those sources, with citations. Also makes audio summaries. One of the easiest ways for a busy executive to get value quickly.

resources.title: Perplexity
resources.author: Perplexity AI
resources.description: An answer engine that searches the web and cites its sources. A low-risk first habit for leaders: use it in place of a search engine for a week.

resources.title: Arena (formerly LMArena)
resources.author: Arena
resources.description: A leaderboard built from blind head-to-head votes between models, for text, code and images. Also lets you compare two models on your own prompt. A quick sense check on vendor claims.

resources.title: Artificial Analysis
resources.author: Artificial Analysis
resources.description: Independent benchmarks comparing models and API providers on capability, speed and price. Useful in procurement and when a team proposes switching model.
